campaign: Gen 7.1 · independent policy comparison and Gen6/BEN anchors
interpretation: Gen 7.1 against Gen 7: the same bot with policy net v4.1 against itself with v4, so the result is what the new net is worth in play; and Gen 7.1 against Gen 6 fast as the generation comparison. Common and native auctions are separate conditions; both bots bid alike, so identical auctions reuse physical games. Only unplayed source deals are allocated. Intervals are descriptive and unadjusted for repeated monitoring.
model_note: Gen 7.1 standard (71s-32) is Gen 7 standard with policy net v4.1 in place of v4; nothing else differs. Gen 7 standard (7s-32) is Gen 6 fast (6-32: same bidder, lead net, hand-fit scorer, layouts and 32 samples) with the gen7 engine (bridge_harness/gen7.py) and policy net v4: layouts weighted by the play so far from trick 7, exact ties broken by the net, and at tricks 3 to 6 a tree search over the net's likeliest cards that re-values the cards the search rates within 0.25 tricks of its best (trust 0.3, stake rule at 0.5 IMPs, at most 3 tricks, 8 layouts). Settings are in the bot's `gen7` block. Every other bot is unchanged from the source run. docs/gen7_alpha_2026-11-11.md has the details.

difference_definition.unit: IMPs per board, candidate minus opponent
difference_definition.bidding: Native minus common on the same board; includes auction/play interaction
difference_definition.uncertainty: Student-t intervals on paired per-board differences; exploratory, unadjusted for repeated monitoring
